title: What Building Shippy Taught Us About Building Agents
hook: When a wrong answer can send a patrol boat miles off course, Ai2's maritime agent Shippy leans on deterministic tools and sandboxed sessions instead of hoping the model behaves.
key_points: Shippy is Ai2 Skylight's maritime-awareness agent, serving 300+ partners across 70+ countries on vessel-activity and boundary questions.
Design splits into 'soul' (system prompt = persona/boundaries), 'skills' (markdown task handlers), and 'config' (model/harness settings).
Instead of raw API calls, Shippy talks to a purpose-built CLI with rich --help/errors — raw calls once caused silent pagination and geometry bugs.
'Mothership' gives each user session its own Kubernetes pod with scoped credentials, so a session's files never leak across users.
Static benchmarks miss real agent behavior, so the team built custom evals: expert-written scenarios and rubrics graded on live data.
Real failures found: tactical overreach in patrol planning, boundary-simplification errors, and one invented, nonexistent CLI command.
content_html: Shippy is Ai2 Skylight's agent for real-time maritime domain awareness — answering questions about vessel activity, fishing events, and protected-area boundaries for government agencies and NGOs across 70+ countries, where a wrong answer could send a patrol boat miles off course. The team's write-up distills what shipping a high-stakes agent like this actually required.
extra_html: The Skylight team frames an agent as three separable pieces: a "soul" (the system prompt setting persona and hard boundaries — Shippy won't make legal determinations about whether a vessel is breaking the law, for instance), "skills" (markdown files that handle specific request types), and "config" (runtime settings like which model or harness to run). That split makes swapping models a config change rather than a rewrite. Two more lessons stand out: give a nondeterministic model deterministic tools — Shippy calls a purpose-built CLI with self-documenting errors rather than constructing Skylight API calls itself, after early prototypes that did so directly produced silent pagination drops and geometry bugs — and isolate every session, via "Mothership," a platform that spins up a dedicated Kubernetes pod with scoped credentials per user. Because static benchmarks don't capture real agent behavior, the team also built custom evals — expert-written scenarios and rubrics scored against live data — which surfaced concrete failures like tactical overreach in patrol planning and one invented, nonexistent CLI command. Ai2 Skylight Team, Hugging Face blog, July 2026.

related.title: Claude Agent Skills
related.hook: Agent Skills package instructions, scripts, and resources into folders an agent loads on demand — composable, portable expertise, later opened as a standard like MCP.

related.title: Model Context Protocol (MCP): A Standard for Connecting LLMs to Tools
related.hook: MCP is an open protocol that standardizes how AI applications expose tools, data, and resources to models - think USB-C for AI tool integrations.

flashcards.prompt: How does the Shippy team split an agent's design into three parts?
flashcards.back_html: "Soul" (the system prompt defining persona and boundaries), "skills" (markdown files handling specific request types), and "config" (model/harness settings) — so swapping a model is a config change, not a rebuild.

flashcards.prompt: Why does Shippy talk to a purpose-built CLI instead of constructing Skylight API calls itself?

choices.text: Letting the agent build raw API calls caused silent pagination drops and geometry encoding errors
The Skylight API has no documentation at all
CLIs are always faster than direct API calls
Direct API access is against Ai2's usage policy

flashcards.explanation_html: Early prototypes that let the agent build API calls directly produced malformed pagination and geometry errors, so the team put a CLI with rich --help text and clear errors between the agent and the API.

flashcards.prompt: What does 'Mothership' do for Shippy's user sessions?
flashcards.back_html: It provisions a dedicated Kubernetes pod per user session with scoped credentials, so files from one analyst's session are never shared with another user's.

flashcards.prompt: What real failure mode did Shippy's custom evals catch, beyond boundary and geometry issues?

choices.text: The agent invented a CLI command that didn't actually exist
The agent refused to answer any maritime question
The agent leaked one user's session data to another user

flashcards.explanation_html: Among the failure modes the eval suite surfaced was tactical overreach in patrol planning and one case where the agent hallucinated a nonexistent CLI command.
